gris-lectura.note: Declared as --color-skin-muted. Secondary prose, taglines, addresses.

gris-ficha.note: Declared as --color-skin-dimmed. The register's metadata voice: dates, venues, eyebrows, breadcrumbs.

papel.note: Declared as --color-skin-inverted. Every content surface, and all reversed type over photography.

negro-sala.note: The fixed navigation bar, and nothing else. Never used for body text.

azul-archivo.note: Tailwind sky-700. The system's only accent; interactive elements exclusively. 5.93:1 on white — replaced sky-600 (#0284c7), which measured 4.10:1 and failed WCAG AA.

azul-archivo-hover.note: Tailwind sky-800. Hovered/pressed state of the accent. 7.56:1 on white.

azul-regla.note: Tailwind sky-500, exposed as --color-skin-rule. Structural only: the active-nav underline, the mobile active left border, and the focus ring on the black bar. Stays sky-500 because on Negro Sala it measures 7.58:1 where the accent manages 3.54:1.

azul-sala.note: Tailwind sky-800. Background of the active item in the mobile menu only.

linea-division.note: Tailwind gray-200. The system's single horizontal rule, above the previous/next pair.

velo-claro.note: Tailwind gray-300, applied only as a mix-blend-multiply scrim over the home hero photograph.

velo-denso.note: Tailwind gray-600, applied only as a mix-blend-multiply scrim over full-bleed decorative sections.

display.purpose: Page titles, presenter names on event pages, home-page section headings. Steps 2.25rem → 3rem → 3.75rem across sm and lg.

headline.purpose: Gallery section headings and the session date in an event header.

title.purpose: Presenter names in card grids and in the previous/next pair.

lead.purpose: Session taglines and the standfirst under a page title, set in Gris Lectura.

body.purpose: Running prose. Long-form pages use prose md:prose-lg lg:prose-xl at max-w-prose.

label.purpose: Uppercase eyebrows, card dates, breadcrumbs. Always Gris Ficha. The only role that is uppercased.

credit.purpose: The © line under every photograph. 700 weight, full-strength ink — content, not chrome.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Under gallery photographs (shadow-xs). Barely perceptible; separates a light image from white paper.

shadows.name: ficha
shadows.purpose: Cover images in the archive grid (shadow-md). The one place a card reads as an object.

motion.name: cover-zoom
motion.purpose: Cover image scales to 1.05 inside its overflow-hidden frame on card hover. The system's only substantive motion.

motion.name: menu-enter
motion.purpose: Mobile menu reveal, driven by data-transition-* attributes on the mobile-menu Stimulus controller.

motion.name: scroll-smooth
motion.purpose: Set on the root element for in-page anchors.

notes: Tailwind CSS 4, theme-in-CSS. There is no tailwind.config.js; --color-skin-* tokens live in frontend/styles/config.css inside an @theme block and generate text-/bg-/border-skin-* utilities.
FONT GAP: only Oswald 600 is self-hosted, while every heading requests font-bold (700). 700 is normative; the fix is shipping oswald-v49-latin-700.

ACCENT: --color-skin-accented / -hover in frontend/styles/config.css are the single source of truth (#0369a1 / #075985). They previously held an unused emerald while templates hard-coded a below-AA sky-600; do not reintroduce raw sky-* utilities for accent text or fills.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The archive's single button — the call through to the full listing of sessions. Every other action in the system is a text link.

narrative.overview:
f/64 is a public register of thirty evenings that already happened. The interface is a catalogue card, not a poster: every session carries a date, a venue, a presenter, and a credit, and the design's job is to make those four facts unambiguous and permanent. The structure is visible on purpose — that legibility is the aesthetic. Nothing here is persuading anyone of anything, because there is nothing left to attend.

Around that spine, the system is almost entirely absent. Two families, one accent, white surfaces, near-square corners, and no ornament that isn't a photograph. Depth is a photographic property rather than a UI one: full-bleed images run the height of the viewport, held under a gray multiply scrim so display type can sit on top of them, and parallax arrives only from background-attachment: fixed above md. Box-shadows exist but are vestigial — 1px hairlines under photographs that could disappear tomorrow without the system noticing.

The tension that keeps it from being bland is scale. Oswald runs to 3.75rem on a page whose body copy is 1rem, and dates are set at the same size as names — a session's date is a headline here, not metadata. Photographs are laid out asymmetrically (the first image in every set spans two of three columns), so a gallery reads as a considered sequence rather than a contact sheet.
keyCharacteristics: Photography is the only decoration; the interface has none of its own.
Dates are set as headlines, at display scale, because the archive is organized by them.
Flat surfaces throughout — depth comes from full-bleed imagery and multiply scrims.
Near-square corners on the work (2px), gently rounded on navigation objects (6px).
One accent, sky blue, reserved almost entirely for links and interactive state.
Credit lines are typographically emphasized (700 weight) and never treated as caption filler.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Azul Archivo marks what is interactive and nothing else. It is never a decorative fill, never a background for a section, never applied to a heading that isn't a link. If a blue element cannot be clicked, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Scrim-Only Rule
rules.body: Gray is never a surface color. The two grays that touch large areas exist exclusively as mix-blend-multiply overlays on photographs, and only where type must sit on top. A photograph carrying no text carries no scrim.

rules.name: The Ink Is Not Black Rule
rules.body: Body copy is Tinta Indígo (#1f1b36), never #000. Pure black in this system means the navigation bar. Using it for text collapses the distinction.

rules.name: The Date Is A Headline Rule
rules.body: In an archive organized by date, the date is not metadata. On the home page and every event page it is set in Oswald at headline scale or larger, and it is wrapped in a <time datetime> carrying the machine-readable ISO value derived by the builder.

rules.name: The Credit Is Not Caption Rule
rules.body: A photograph's © line is set at 700 weight in full-strength ink, never in Gris Ficha, never italicized, never smaller than 0.875rem. It is content, not chrome, and it may not be moved out of the image's immediate vicinity.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is For Labels Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for the 0.875rem–1.25rem label role. Headings are never uppercased; Oswald is already condensed enough that uppercase display type turns into a wall.

rules.name: The Hero Photo Is Asymmetric Rule
rules.body: In any gallery of three or more, the first figure spans two of three columns (sm:col-span-2) and the rest are single. A photo set is a sequence with an opening image, never a uniform grid.

rules.name: The Parallax Stops At md Rule
rules.body: bg-fixed is applied only above md (bg-scroll md:bg-fixed). Fixed backgrounds repaint on every scroll frame and are a known source of mobile jank.

rules.name: The Photograph Is The Elevation Rule
rules.body: When a section needs depth, it gets a photograph — full-bleed, scrimmed, and parallaxed above md. It does not get a shadow, a gradient, or a tinted panel. There are no new shadow tokens to invent here.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 2px for the work, 6px for the interface. Nothing in this system is rounded-full, rounded-xl, or larger — a pill or a heavily rounded panel reads as product UI and breaks the register.

rules.name: The Register States Its Own Closure Rule
rules.body: Every event page says which session it is (Sesión N de 30), which year it belongs to (a breadcrumb step linking to that year's anchor), and that the cycle ended. Visitors land deep, so a fact that lives only on the index is a fact most of them never see.

dos: Do render every image through _partials/_picture.erb, passing all four locals (src, alt, classes, eager) — Bridgetown raises on undefined ones, and the partial is what supplies WebP, intrinsic dimensions, and the loading strategy.
Do attach a © credit to every photograph, at 700 weight in full-strength ink, immediately below the image.
Do wrap dates in <time datetime="…"> using the ISO value the events builder derives, and set them in Oswald at headline scale or larger.
Do reach for the skin-* token utilities (text-skin-base, text-skin-muted, text-skin-dimmed, text-skin-inverted) for text color.
Do give the first figure in any three-or-more gallery sm:col-span-2.
Do pair bg-scroll md:bg-fixed on any full-bleed background, and mark the section aria-hidden="true" when the photograph is decorative.
Do keep the accent to interactive elements only.
Do give `sizes` the slot's real rendered width, per call site — it is the only thing the partial cannot infer, and a wrong sizes is worse than none.
donts: Don't hard-code a sky-* utility for accent text or fills. --color-skin-accented / -hover (#0369a1 / #075985) are the live, AA-compliant accent; see The Token Is The Accent Rule.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, a gradient, or a tinted section background. White paper, black bar, one blue.
Don't add elevation. If a region needs depth, it gets a scrimmed photograph — see The Photograph Is The Elevation Rule.
Don't round anything past 6px, and never use rounded-full or rounded-xl.
Don't set body text in #000; it is Tinta Indígo (#1f1b36).
Don't dim, shrink, italicize, crop, or relocate a credit line away from its photograph.
Don't uppercase a heading. Uppercase belongs to the label role.
Don't ship an without width/height — the partial supplies them, and going around it reintroduces the layout shift that motivated plugins/builders/images.rb.
Don't write arbitrary-value background utilities for full-bleed imagery; add a .bg-photo-* class at the foot of frontend/styles/index.css so the WebP can be offered through image-set().
Don't state a fact only on the index. /eventos/ is not the page most visitors see.
